projectContext.occupancy: Group R-2 stated by the question
projectContext.configuration: Scissor stair with entrance doors 15 feet apart

exactPassages: Stairs sharing any common wall, floor, ceiling, scissor stair assembly, or other enclosure shall be counted as one exit stairway.

3. Group R-2 occupancies. In Group R-2 occupancies, where stairs are enclosed in walls having at least a 2-hour fire resistance rating and constructed of masonry or masonry equivalent in accordance with department rules: 3.1. testCase.question: Our Group R-2 building has a scissor stair with the two stair entrance doors located 15 feet apart. Can the two stairs be counted as two separate exits?
testCase.expectedConclusion: The 15-foot separation alone is not enough. Under the general rule, stairs sharing a scissor-stair assembly are counted as one exit stairway. However, the Group R-2 exception permits the stairs to share the assembly and be counted separately when the stair enclosures and the construction separating the stairs have at least a 2-hour fire-resistance rating and are constructed of masonry or a masonry equivalent in accordance with department rules. The exit doors must also be at least 15 feet apart. Confirm the occupancy group, enclosure rating, separating construction, and material before concluding that the exception applies.

answer.conclusion: Conditionally yes. Although stairs sharing a scissor stair assembly are generally counted as one exit stairway, Exception 3 for Group R-2 permits them to share a scissor stair assembly and be treated as separate stairs if the stated construction and door-separation conditions are met. The reported 15-foot door separation meets the exception’s minimum only if the distance is at least 15 feet. Final reliance also requires verification that both stair enclosures and the construction separating the stairs have the required 2-hour, masonry-or-masonry-equivalent construction under applicable department rules. [Section 1007.1.1, Passage IDs 5c6159cd-34ae-4941-8dbe-b65c6f533fa0 and 4ccbcebc-da60-4c70-ab54-66e69432da28]
answer.explanation:
The base rule states that stairs sharing a common wall, floor, ceiling, scissor stair assembly, or other enclosure must be counted as one exit stairway. [Section 1007.1.1, Passage ID 5c6159cd-34ae-4941-8dbe-b65c6f533fa0]

Under Exception 3, however, Group R-2 stairs may share common walls, floors, ceilings, scissor stair assemblies, or other enclosures when: (1) the stairs are enclosed by walls with at least a 2-hour fire-resistance rating and are constructed of masonry or masonry equivalent in accordance with department rules; (2) the exit doors to the stairs are at least 15 feet apart; and (3) the construction separating the stairs is also at least 2-hour fire-resistance-rated and masonry or masonry equivalent in accordance with department rules. [Section 1007.1.1, Passage ID 4ccbcebc-da60-4c70-ab54-66e69432da28]

Thus, the stated 15-foot door spacing satisfies the numerical minimum stated in Exception 3.1, subject to confirming the measurement is no less than 15 feet and the remaining construction conditions are satisfied.

testCase.title: Occupancy classification of a residential multipurpose room

exactPassages: A room or space used for assembly purposes with an occupant load of fewer than 75 persons and accessory to another occupancy shall be classified as a Group B occupancy or as part of that occupancy, except that the number of plumbing fixtures for such a room or space is permitted to be calculated in accordance with the requirements for assembly occupancies.

For areas without fixed seating, the occupant load shall be not less than that number determined by dividing the floor area under consideration by the occupant load factor assigned to the function of the space as set forth in Table 1004.1.3.

testCase.question: A 900-net-square-foot multipurpose room in an apartment building will normally contain tables and chairs and is only for residents. Does it need to be classified as Group A-3?
testCase.expectedConclusion: For an unconcentrated assembly arrangement with tables and chairs, Table 1004.1.3 uses 15 net square feet per occupant. A 900-net-square-foot room therefore has a calculated occupant load of 60 people. Because that is fewer than 75 occupants, and assuming the room is accessory to the residential occupancy, BC 303.1.3 permits it to be classified as Group B or as part of the occupancy it serves rather than as Group A. The result depends on the actual net area, furniture arrangement, intended activities, and whether the room is truly accessory to the residential use.

Calculate 900 divided by 15 as an occupant load of 60.

answer.conclusion: Conditionally, no. If the room is an assembly-purpose space, is accessory to the apartment building’s primary occupancy, and its code-calculated occupant load is fewer than 75 persons, it is classified as Group B or as part of the occupancy to which it is accessory—not Group A-3. For the stated normal arrangement of tables and chairs without fixed seating, the selected occupant-load procedure yields 900 net square feet ÷ 15 net square feet/person = 60 persons. Because 60 is fewer than 75, the accessory-assembly provision applies if the accessory relationship is confirmed. The provision separately permits plumbing fixtures for the room to be calculated under assembly-occupancy requirements. [§303.1.3, Passage 81639c15-fe03-479f-afdd-6f23a341d5d5; §1004.1.3, Passages 0d4f1170-a66d-4a73-bb35-3e9f23e7c2c4, fb37f6ec-3b58-46c7-9aac-4166e8d331a4, ae5651aa-0cd5-4a02-ae0d-ae23ac74caae]
answer.explanation: The selected evidence requires occupant load for an area without fixed seating to be determined by dividing the floor area by the Table 1004.1.3 factor assigned to the space’s function. The selected table entry identifies “Unconcentrated (tables and chairs)” with a factor of 15 net square feet per person. Using the stated 900 net square feet: 900 ÷ 15 = 60 occupants. Section 303.1.3 then provides the classification result for an assembly-purpose room or space that has an occupant load of fewer than 75 persons and is accessory to another occupancy. Resident-only use supports, but does not by itself establish from the selected text, that the room is accessory to the apartment building occupancy. exactPassages: A room or space used for assembly purposes with an occupant load of fewer than 75 persons and accessory to another occupancy shall be classified as a Group B occupancy or as part of that occupancy, except that the number of plumbing fixtures for such a room or space is permitted to be calculated in accordance with the requirements for assembly occupancies.

Plumbing fixtures shall be provided for the type of occupancy and in the minimum number shown in Table 403.1. Types of occupancies not shown in Table 403.1 shall be considered individually by the commissioner. The number of occupants shall be determined by the New York City Building Code. Occupancy classification shall be determined in accordance with the New York City Building Code.

The number of fixtures for building or nonaccessory tenant space used for assembly purposes by fewer than 75 persons and classified as Group B occupancy in accordance with Section 303.1, Exception 2 of the New York City Building Code shall be permitted to be calculated in accordance with the requirements for Assembly occupancies.

To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. To determine the required number of fixtures, the fixture ratio or ratios for each fixture type shall be applied to the occupant load of each sex in accordance with Table 403.1. Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number. Fixture calculations in Group B office occupancies shall utilize the total occupant load on a given floor to determine the number of fixtures required for that floor.
Exception: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.
